cases.reviewerAnswer: Tengo un coche; tengo una hermana; ¿Tienes perro?; Ana tiene un piso nuevo; Ana tiene el pelo largo.
el calor; heat; tener calor means to feel hot.
el frío; cold; tener frío means to feel cold.
el pelo; hair collectively; Ana tiene el pelo largo.
cases.notes: The singular explanation fits the collective meaning taught here; it need not introduce individual hairs, pelos.

cases.reviewerAnswer: la sed; thirst; tener sed means to be thirsty.
el sueño; sleepiness or sleep; plural sueños; tener sueño means to be sleepy.
tener means to have; tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen.
The tener paradigm and the possession and physical-state examples are correct. Article omission with tener is also possible in affirmative clauses.

cases.reviewerAnswer: Tengo un hermano y una hermana. Optional explicit yo.
Sí, tengo coche. Also: Sí, tengo un coche, with optional yo.
Tengo un gato y un perro. Optional yo; reversing the animal order preserves the meaning.
Tenemos calor. Optional nosotros or nosotras.
¿Tenéis sed? In familiar western Andalusian ustedes usage, ¿Tienen sed? can also fit.
cases.element: task.errors[id=e2].feedbackUk: 'Tienen — для ellos або ввічливого ustedes; друзям на «ти» — ¿Tenéis sed?'
cases.defect: The intended plural address system is unspecified. The feedback fits the vosotros system, but familiar ustedes also occurs in parts of mainland Spain. Spain Spanish alone does not establish that ustedes must be formal.
cases.correction: Specify that this exercise requires the vosotros system. Alternatively, acknowledge familiar regional ustedes usage and assess that answer accordingly.
sources: Course contract rule 8 and the verdict instruction concerning unspecified regional acceptability.
